name: Cubism
summary: Analytic-cubist canvas: a warm cream ground broken into offset charcoal-edged planes of ochre, olive, warm gray, and blue-gray, one form drawn from several viewpoints at once, with flat papier collé cuts instead of shadows or gradients.
whenToUse: When the user asks for Cubism, Picasso/Braque, fragmented planes, multiple viewpoints, papier collé collage, muted modernist earth tones, angular editorial layouts, or a gallery/museum-catalogue aesthetic — and for any interface that should read as constructed from cut planes rather than floating cards.
rules: Compose in planes, not boxes: every surface is an irregular quadrilateral or a chevron cut from the cream ground, sitting at a 3–12° tilt off the orthogonal so the page reads as a constructed picture rather than a stack of rectangles.

Show more than one viewpoint: give any hero form, illustration, or subject two overlapping readings (a front profile plus a side edge, a disc plus its rim), because simultaneity is the whole argument of the style.

Zero radius, zero blur: corners are 0px and hard-edged, depth comes from overlapping opaque planes with a 2px #2a2a28 edge and a 6px 6px 0 #8a7f6f offset, and no shadow, glow, gradient, or translucent wash is ever allowed — Cubist light is even, not directional.

Spend one earth tone per plane and one role color per component: ochre #b08d57 for primary action, blue-gray #5b6b7a for links, focus, and secondary action, olive #6b6b3e for confirmed/success, #8f3b2f for failure, warm gray #8a7f6f for muted labels and paste shadows.

Set display type in Archivo Black, uppercase or Title Case, 20px and up, tracking 0 to 0.04em, with headings broken across two lines and offset in x by 8–24px so the typography itself fractures; never let a heading sit in a perfect single-line block.

Body copy is Archivo 400/500 at 16–18px/1.55 in charcoal; IBM Plex Mono is reserved for catalogue data — accession numbers, dimensions, dates, editions — and is the only place numerals get a fixed-width grid.

Keep text in charcoal #2a2a28 or cream #efe9dc on the earth fills; ochre, olive, warm gray, and blue-gray carry text only at 18px and up with a 700 weight, otherwise they are fields, edges, and cut shapes.

Animate as re-cutting, not as movement: 160–240ms cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1) transforms that shift one facet's clip-path or offset by 4–8px, one overshoot-free settle, and never a fade, spin, parallax, or floating loop.

Stay evocation-only: no reproduced painting, sketch, or museum artwork, no signature, no logo — the style is carried by palette, planar composition, collage edges, and multiple-viewpoint drawing made from primitives.

componentRecipes.panel: position: relative; background: #f5f1e8; color: #2a2a28; border: 2px solid #2a2a28; border-radius: 0; padding: 24px; clip-path: polygon(0 10px, 10px 0, 100% 0, 100% calc(100% - 20px), calc(100% - 20px) 100%, 0 100%); box-shadow: 6px 6px 0 #8a7f6f; — add one offset ::before plane behind it: background #b08d57, clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 24% 100%, 0 62%), transform: translate(-12px, 10px), z-index: -1, opacity 1 (never translucent); a panel that is the catalogue subject gets a second blue-gray #5b6b7a facet pinned to its top-right corner at 18% width; heading inside is Archivo Black 24px/1.05 Title Case with the first word shifted left 8px; below 640px keep the 2px edge and drop the hard offset.
componentRecipes.button: font: 700 16px/1 'Archivo Black', 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; padding: 14px 24px 14px 20px; background: #b08d57; color: #2a2a28; border: 2px solid #2a2a28; border-radius: 0; clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 14px 100%, 0 calc(100% - 14px)); box-shadow: 6px 6px 0 #2a2a28; transition: transform 160ms cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1), background-color 160ms linear; :hover { background: #c19a63; transform: translate(-2px, -2px); box-shadow: 8px 8px 0 #2a2a28; } :active { background: #9a7a49; transform: translate(4px, 4px); box-shadow: 2px 2px 0 #2a2a28; } :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #5b6b7a; outline-offset: 4px; } — secondary variant: background #efe9dc, color #2a2a28, box-shadow 6px 6px 0 #8a7f6f; disabled: background #d9cfba, color #8a7f6f, border-color #8a7f6f, box-shadow 0 0 0, no clip-path change and no transform.
componentRecipes.input: font: 16px/1.5 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; color: #2a2a28; background: #efe9dc; border: 2px solid #2a2a28; border-left-width: 10px; border-left-color: #8a7f6f; border-radius: 0; padding: 12px 16px; clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 10px 100%, 0 calc(100% - 10px)); box-shadow: none; :placeholder { color: #8a7f6f; font: 400 14px 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.02em; } :focus { background: #f5f1e8; border-left-color: #5b6b7a; outline: 2px solid #5b6b7a; outline-offset: 2px; } — invalid: border-color #8f3b2f with a 16px Archivo sentence below in #8f3b2f ('This field needs a value.') plus a 2px #8f3b2f edge, so the error never depends on color alone.
componentRecipes.statusbar: height: 48px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 24px; padding: 0 24px; background: #efe9dc; border-top: 2px solid #2a2a28; border-radius: 0; font: 13px/1.4 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: #2a2a28; the left block is a row of mono labels separated by 2px #2a2a28 vertical rules and each preceded by an 8px clip-path parallelogram in the state color — #6b6b3e settled, #b08d57 in progress, #8f3b2f failed, #8a7f6f idle; the right block is a catalogue counter (e.g. 'PL. 014 / 038') plus the single primary action; the in-progress marker shifts its clip-path 3° over 240ms cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1) once, no looping pulse.
componentRecipes.menu: vertical facet list, no bullets, 4px gap: item { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; padding: 12px 20px; font: 700 17px/1.3 'Archivo Black', 'Archivo Narrow', system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.02em; color: #2a2a28; background: #f5f1e8; border: 2px solid #2a2a28; border-radius: 0; clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% calc(100% - 12px), calc(100% - 12px) 100%, 0 100%); } the selected item fills #b08d57 and gains a 10px charcoal triangle marker in clip-path on its left edge, hover shifts background to #e8e1d2 and translates the row translate(-4px, 0); group headers are IBM Plex Mono 12px uppercase with letter-spacing 0.16em on the cream ground with a 2px #8a7f6f underline that stops at 40% width.
componentRecipes.toggle: faceted switch, 76px x 36px: track { background: #d9cfba; border: 2px solid #2a2a28; border-radius: 0; padding: 0; clip-path: polygon(8px 0, 100% 0, calc(100% - 8px) 100%, 0 100%); } knob is a 30px tall parallelogram with a 2px #2a2a28 edge, #5b6b7a when off and #6b6b3e when on, sliding 34px over 240ms cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1) with a 3° skew that stays constant so the knob reads as a cut facet; label sits above in Archivo 700 14px Title Case and the state is repeated as text ('Off'/'On') beside the track for screen readers.

copywriting.voice: Atelier-notebook voice with a gallery wall label's precision: observant, declarative, a little analytical, never precious. Copy describes what is seen and what is being built ('Two viewpoints, one object. We kept the edge that disagreed.') rather than selling a product — the reader is a collaborator in a studio, not a customer in a funnel.

case.commands: sentence case imperative ('Pin the plane', 'Show the second view')

avoid: gallery gatekeeping jargon used to exclude ('problematic', 'praxis', 'liminal') and untranslated art-history name-dropping
deadpan system errors ('Invalid input.', 'An error occurred')
emoji as bullets, icons, or inside headings
all-caps sentences longer than three words
any claim that the work is by, after, or in the style of a named living artist

do: Break the rectangle: give each major surface a tilted or chamfered clip-path so no two adjacent containers share a parallel edge angle.
Draw every subject from at least two viewpoints — a profile plus its side, a disc plus its rim — and let the planes overlap rather than reconcile.
Keep the ground warm cream #efe9dc with cards at #f5f1e8, and let only the earth palette (ochre, olive, warm gray, blue-gray, sand, charcoal) sit on it.
Edge every plane with 2px #2a2a28 and lift it with a single hard 6px 6px 0 #8a7f6f offset; nothing in the system is blurred.
Fracture the type: split headings across two lines and offset them 8–24px so the text participates in the composition instead of captioning it.
Hold one strict 12-column grid under the chaos — the planes cut across columns, but the columns never move — so the collision looks constructed, not accidental.
dont: No artworks: no reproduced painting, drawing, print, sketch, signature, or museum image — evocation comes from palette, planar composition, and collage primitives only.
No gradients, glows, blurs, backdrop-filter, or semi-transparent overlays; Cubist light is flat and even, one opaque fill per plane.
No rounded corners, no pills, no 1px hairlines — radius is 0 and the minimum edge weight is 2px #2a2a28.
No floating-card dashboard: if every element is a horizontal rectangle with a soft shadow, the style has collapsed into generic minimalism.
No decorative second earth tone inside one component; one role color per plane, plus charcoal for the edge and the text.
No bounce, parallax, spin, shimmer, or infinite loops; motion is a single 160–240ms re-cut and then stillness.
No faux-old-paper texture over photographs or illustrations, and no sepia filter applied to real imagery — the palette is drawn, not aged.
accessibility: Charcoal #2a2a28 on cream #efe9dc clears 4.5:1 and cream on charcoal is stronger still; ochre #b08d57, olive #6b6b3e, warm gray #8a7f6f, and blue-gray #5b6b7a do not carry small text — use them as fields, edges, and cut shapes, or set text inside them at 18px+ in charcoal (ochre) or cream (blue-gray, olive).

Archivo Black is display-only: 20px minimum for headings, never a paragraph, and never a form value; body copy stays Archivo 400/500 at 16px+ with 1.5 line-height, and IBM Plex Mono stays at 13px+ for catalogue data.
Tilted planes must not tilt text: keep every text block axis-aligned and horizontal inside its rotated or clipped facet, and cap container tilt at 12° so line-length and baseline stay predictable.
Honor prefers-reduced-motion: replace the facet re-cut with an instant state change and remove the clip-path shift entirely — the state must remain readable with zero animation.

Never signal state with earth color alone — pair each plane, edge, and marker with a word ('Settled', 'In progress', 'Failed') and a visible 2px #5b6b7a focus ring offset 4px on every focusable element.
Keep scroll order equal to visual order when planes overlap; if a facet is decorative, mark it aria-hidden so screen readers get the text, not the collage.
signatureElement: The fractured plane: a single form rebuilt from offset charcoal-edged quadrilaterals in ochre, olive, warm gray, and blue-gray, its facets showing two viewpoints at once and never resolving into one outline

prose.overview: This mode stages the interface as an analytic-cubist canvas: a warm cream ground, ochre and olive planes cut across it at slight angles, charcoal edges, and one subject drawn from two viewpoints at once. Nothing floats and nothing glows — surfaces overlap, disagree at their edges, and still hold a strict grid underneath, so the page reads as a constructed picture rather than a stack of cards. It is muted, intellectual, and a little severe: the reward for looking is that the composition resolves, not that something shines. Use it when the work should feel studied, editorial, and hand-built rather than fast and frictionless.
prose.colors: The ground is cream #efe9dc with cards one step lighter at #f5f1e8, and charcoal #2a2a28 draws every edge and carries nearly all text. The palette is deliberately narrow and earthen: ochre #b08d57 for the primary action, blue-gray #5b6b7a for links, focus, and secondary action, olive #6b6b3e for a settled or successful state, #8f3b2f for hard failure, sand #d9cfba for wells and paste shadows, and warm gray #8a7f6f for muted labels and lifted offsets. Every plane is one opaque fill — no alpha, no gradient, no directional light — because Cubist space is described by the shifting relationship of planes, not by a lamp. The earth ramps give each hue a light/base/dark triad for hover and pressed states, so shading happens through palette steps rather than through blur.
prose.typography: Archivo Black leads at 20px and up in Title Case or uppercase, and the type is treated as part of the collage: headings break across two lines and offset 8–24px in x so they fracture the same way the planes do. Body copy drops to Archivo 400/500 at 16–18px with 1.55 line-height in charcoal, kept axis-aligned inside tilted containers so readability survives the composition. IBM Plex Mono is reserved for catalogue data — accession numbers, dimensions, dates, editions — where its fixed rhythm makes the numerals feel archival. No script, no humanist serif, and no decorative display face is admitted; the style's drama comes from scale and placement, not from letterform ornament.
prose.layout: Layout is a 12-column editorial grid in a 4/8/16/24/40px scale, with 24px gutters and generous margins, over which planes are cut at 3–12° off the orthogonal. Composition is asymmetric by rule: a large subject plane holds two-thirds of the first viewport, a narrow column of text sits against it, and the remaining space is one quiet facet of ground rather than filler. Sections advance as plates in a catalogue — each has a mono plate number, a title, and a single dominant plane — and the left-to-right reading order is never broken even where facets overlap. On narrow screens the tilt reduces to 3° and the planes stack, but their chamfered corners and offset edges are kept so the construction is still legible.
prose.elevation: Depth is collage depth, not light: planes overlap, each carrying a 2px #2a2a28 edge, and lift with a single hard 6px 6px 0 #8a7f6f offset that behaves like a pasted shadow rather than a cast one. There is no blur, no ambient occlusion, no glow, and no translucent veil anywhere in the system; internal depth is expressed by a filled inset block in sand #d9cfba or by an offset ::before plane in ochre. Pressing an element moves it into its offset (translate(4px,4px) with the shadow closing to 2px) so the gesture reads as a cut paper being pushed flat. Z-order is composition: the smallest plane is always on top, and the charcoal edge is what lets a viewer know where one facet ends.
prose.shapes: Shapes are angular and asymmetric — chamfered quadrilaterals, chevrons, wedges, and skewed parallelograms made with clip-path — all at 0px radius, outlined at 2px charcoal, and tilted a few degrees so no two neighbours share an angle. Motifs are built from primitives: a disc for a face, a profile wedge for a nose, a cylinder stripe for a bottle, an offset trapezoid for a tabletop, a tape strip for a collage join, and a small triangle for a viewer's mark. Edges are visibly cut — a corner clipped 10–20px, a facet stepping out 4px — and a straight rectangle with a soft shadow is treated as a failure of the style. There are no circles except the motif disc, no curves in container geometry, and no ornament that does not derive from a plane.
prose.components: Cards are cream facets with a 2px charcoal edge, a chamfered bottom-right corner, and a 6px hard warm-gray offset, often with a single ochre plane pinned behind them. Buttons are angular ochre cuts that lose their offset under the press, with a cream-stroked secondary that keeps a warm-gray shadow so it still reads as a plane rather than a ghost. Inputs are cream wells with a 10px thick left edge that turns blue-gray on focus and charcoal otherwise, set in IBM Plex Mono so values look catalogued, and toggles are faceted parallelogram knobs sliding along a skewed track. The status bar is a catalogue strip — mono labels split by 2px rules, each with an 8px state parallelogram, an edition counter, and the single primary action at the right.
prose.dosDonts: Do break every rectangle with a clip-path, show two viewpoints of any subject, keep one opaque earth fill per plane, and let headings and planes disagree by a few degrees. Don't reproduce any artwork, drawing, or signature, don't soften the construction with gradients or blur, don't tilt running text, and don't trade the grid for the collage — the tension between them is the entire effect.
